Mr. Katyal claimed this ambiguity is impermissible under the Eighth Amendment.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case concerns jury instructions in a death penalty trial. The instructions told jurors how to weigh evidence that might reduce the sentence. The parties disagree on whether these instructions were clear enough to satisfy federal constitutional standards.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines how clearly states must explain jury instructions in death penalty trials. It affects whether jurors can properly weigh evidence that might spare a defendant's life. Clear instructions protect the right to a fair sentencing process.
